meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means employ .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means every .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means preserve .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means rejoice .

This radical is the same as the kanji, but you learned that a really long time ago, so here's a reminder of the mnemonic, just in case: What sticks to your rib cage in the winter? Wheat ! Wheat bread, Wheaties, and cream of wheat make for the ultimate winter survival diet.

Your fingers have to stand up straight, to protect you from being abduct ed, or pull ed away against your will. Hints You're convinced someone is trying to abduct you, so you need to keep your fingers standing at all times, ready to defend yourself. Your fingers are feeling pretty stiff, but you still keep them standing, just in case.
readingMnemonic: Suddenly, someone really is trying to abduct you. They're pull ling you away. It's the ancient Egyptian god Ra ( ら ). Help! Hints Luckily, your fingers were standing to attention and you were able to fight off the mighty Ra. He won't try to abduct you again in a hurry. Thank goodness for those standing fingers.

meaningMnemonic: Every winter you are alert for danger. Everyone knows that the worst monsters come out in the winter so you need to be alert if you want to survive. Hints Imagine yourself out in the winter wilderness. You hear twigs snapping, growling, leaves rustling. You’re incredibly alert and aware of everything going on around you.
readingMnemonic: Being the alert fellow you are, you hear a sasquatch approaching and dive into a trash bin ( びん ) to hide. The bin smells really bad and you are keenly alert to all the various stenches and smells currently penetrating your nostrils, but at least you are safe. Hints Listen to the sasquatch rumble on by as you continue to smell the smelly smells of this putrid bin you’re in.

meaningMnemonic: You attempt to expel wind out of your mouth but lack the breath to blow out any. You’re using your mouth and trying to blow out some air, but you are failing to do so. Hints Blow some air out of your mouth. It’s easy, right? Imagine what could cause you to fail at this activity.
readingMnemonic: You silly foo l ( ふ ), the reason you couldn’t blow any air out of your mouth is because your hand was over it. You can’t blow air out that way. You silly fool, you. Hints Attempt to blow air out of your mouth while covering it with your hand. It’s hard to do, right? Only a fool would try to blow air out of their mouth this way.

meaningMnemonic: It's time to do the mouth sun sun chant . That's when you use your mouth to chant sun sun, sun sun, sun sun, over and over until the sun appears. Hints Open your mouth and practice the chant right now! Sun sun, sun sun, sun sun!
readingMnemonic: You're doing this chant because the Shou gun ( しょう ) ordered you to. The sun hasn't been shining on him as much lately, and he's displeased. So now you have to chant for him. Hints The Shougun is glaring intently at you as you chant. Open your mouth as wide as you can, get all those "sun suns" out, and pray that the sun will appear.

meaningMnemonic: If you try to go somewhere but you're too heavy you'll collide with everything. Cars, people, houses. You're too heavy to dodge them, so you collide with it all. Hints Imagine being too heavy to go anywhere without colliding with things.
readingMnemonic: You're going around the town, you collide with a bunch of things, when all of a sudden you collide with the Shou gun ( しょう )! Oh no! The shogun looks really mad. Hints The Shougun is glaring at you from the ground. "You've been colliding with my entire city and now you collide into ME?!" Smoke blows out his nostrils.

meaningMnemonic: The drunkard issued twenty commandment s to his people. Hints He basically just made up a bunch of commandments to order all the other drunkards around and decided having twenty (twice the amount of that other religion he heard about) would be a good number.
readingMnemonic: The drunkard is yelling out his twenty commandment s to the others at the bar, but they're all about kay aks ( かい ). Hints Commandment 1: Thou shalt not touch my kayak Commandment 2: Thou shalt not look at my kayak Commandment 3: Thou shalt give me beer to put in my kayak It goes on like that for a while...

meaningMnemonic: The Mona Lisa is in front of you. "You must all paint the Mona Lisa concurrently ," says your art class teacher. Hints Pay close attention to the students around you. Don't go too fast or too slow, or you won't finish concurrently.
readingMnemonic: Your entire class finishes concurrently . You look at your finished result. Wait, that's not the Mona Lisa. You painted Ken ( けん ) the samurai. Hints It's a nice painting, the frown is just right, and you finished concurrently with everyone else, but you're probably going to fail this class.

meaningMnemonic: The flowers are being worked upon by a tsunami with a drop specialty : this tsunami can dilute flowers with just one tsunami-powered drop of itself. That’s its specialty. Hints Look at the flowers as the tsunami begins to dilute them with just one drop. Their color and fragrance and dimensions become weaker and more spread out. It’s really trippy to witness.
readingMnemonic: You watch the flowers become dilute d with just one drop, and realize that this is a nature hack ( はく ). You’ve never seen anything like this before, so you think the tsunami found out how to hack nature and that’s how it got so good at diluting things. By hacking nature. Hints As you continue to watch the tsunami's drop of water dilute the flowers, imagine what techniques this tsunami is using to hack nature. Is the tsunami a sinister being from the future? Maybe.

meaningMnemonic: Imagine you're driving and there's some dirt with a flag in it near the exit ramp. That flag marks a ditch running alongside the road. Don't try to exit the road here, or you'll end up stuck in that ditch. Hints Picture the flag in the dirt. Picture the ditch just beyond it. Now look for another way to exit this road, unless you have a ditch wish.
readingMnemonic: If you do end up veering into a ditch you'll find yourself yelling, " Holy ( ほり ) crap!" Then you'll go hurtling into the ditch. Hints It's a pun, get it? Holy. Hole-y. The ditch is a long hole. See? It's funny.

meaningMnemonic: Simultaneous ly, you throw your knife at another person who's throwing a knife at you and you both get a dose of your own medicine. Literally, there's poison on these knives and now you've both been stabbed. Hints Watch as the dose of poison sinks into your body through the knife that's in your chest, as it simultaneously happens to the other guy too.
readingMnemonic: "I need a dose of the antidote!" you yell, and the other guy looks you dead in the eyes. They slowly pull a tiny xy lophone ( ざい ) out of their pocket, play a few notes, and then eat it. "Ah, you'd like a dose of the xylophone cure, wouldn't you?" Hints Now you're begging them for a dose of the xylophone drug. Just a taste, you want to live!

meaningMnemonic: A fang on a turkey is elegant . Most turkeys do not have fangs, so this turkey with a fang is quite elegant and dignified. This turkey is special. Hints Look at this turkey with a fang. It’s elegant, but also frightening. See the fanged turkey staring at you menacingly.
readingMnemonic: This elegant fang makes the turkey look more like a ga rgoyle ( が ) than a turkey. In fact, you haven't seen it move at all. Maybe it is just an elegant gargoyle! Hints Picture this elegant gargoyle sitting in front of you. Reach out your hand and feels its hard, elegant stone gargoyle body.

meaningMnemonic: The fingers are where criminal s emit or expel all of their bad energy from. Hints Picture a criminal’s fingers, and all of the bad energy just oozing out of them, almost like an exhaust pipe emitting toxic fumes.
readingMnemonic: Then you realize what the fingers are actually emit ting: terrible, awful hai ku ( はい ). Hints Imagine this criminal's fingers emitting god-awful, cringe-inducing haiku after haiku. Really feel your skin crawl at the shoddiness of this criminal's fingers' haiku.

meaningMnemonic: Teacher s are all around us. Those who came before us are our teachers, so it's important to respect them. This is the basic idea of filial piety . Hints Respect your elders, for they have much to teach us.
readingMnemonic: With filial piety in mind, you decide to go visit your father, who is こう いち . Hints I am so ignorant and have much to learn. I must show filial piety to my father, こういち , so that he may teach me.

meaningMnemonic: You walk by a geoduck a frequent amount. This geoduck really intrigues you, so you can’t help but frequent the area the geoduck is in and walk around. Hints Imagine walking around near this geoduck. This is the best area to frequent when you want to look at the geoduck. Just keep looking at it as you walk.
readingMnemonic: Apparently Hindu people also love geoducks because Hin du ( ひん ) people frequent this area quite often as well. You always see the geoduck here, but also a lot of Hindu people. Hints Look at all the Hindu people as you walk around and observe the geoduck. Hear them all speaking Hindi as you continue to walk around.

meaningMnemonic: A horse goes to his favorite district to gallop around. This district has lots of cool buildings and lights to look at, so this horse loves to gallop around there. Hints Hear the horse clip clopping around the district as it continues to gallop. Clip clop, clop clip clop!
readingMnemonic: Then the horse gallop s into the road and gets hit by a ca r ( か ). Oh man, there’s blood everywhere. This horse is never going to gallop again. That car totally destroyed it. Hints The tires screech, the horse neighs, BAM! Total destruction everywhere. Bystanders scream in horror. That horse will never gallop again. It’s a sad day for all horsekind.

meaningMnemonic: The leader of all the spider s is a genius ! Spiders are already pretty smart. They can weave complex homes and traps in one web. They even know where not to step so they don't get caught. But the leader knows everything. It made itself a little webbed computer and everything! Hints Imagine seeing the leader of the spiders weaving it's own little spider computer. Doing spider math, and spider chemistry. It's a genius!
readingMnemonic: As you watch the spider genius you realize that soon ( しゅん ) spiders will take over the humans. They're just way smarter than us. Soon we'll be the bugs. Hints Soon we'll be slaves to the genius spiders. Soon we'll be the flies.

meaningMnemonic: A woman is rejoic ing. She must be glad and happy to rejoice out loud in front of you like this. Hints Picture a woman rejoicing loudly. She's got a big smile on her face and she wants you and everyone else to see how glad she is.
readingMnemonic: "I'm so glad !" the woman shouts, "Because I found the key ( き )!" You immediately start to wonder what "the key" is. The key to life? The key to learning Japanese? Then you see she's holding up some car keys. Hints You'd be happy too if you'd just found your lost keys. Though maybe you wouldn't shout it for the entire world to hear.

meaningMnemonic: There’s grass on the ground and the fins there say you have no honor . The fins are left over from the fish you dismembered and they do not believe it was an act of honor. Now they are just sitting on the ground on the grass, calling you out for having no honor. Hints Listen to what the fins have to say as they flop around on the ground in the grass. Hear them swish about as they flop, brushing up against the blades of grass.
readingMnemonic: Being one of little honor , you decide to squash these vocal fins with your yo -yo ( よ ). You take out your yo-yo and start bashing each fin with it until they stop talking about what little honor you have. Hints Imagine taking your yo-yo out to do this. Feel the string tighten around your finger as you unleash the yo-yo and silence all the fins.

meaningMnemonic: A thick carpet of flowers grows on a slide and on the drunkard passed out next to it in your luxuriant garden. Your garden is so luxuriant that the flowers have engulfed literally everything in it, from the kids' play structure to the hapless drunk who wandered in last night. Hints Imagine being in this luxuriant garden — smell the overwhelming floral aroma as you clear flowers off the slide and try to shoo away the drunkard so your kids can come out and play.
readingMnemonic: As you try to shoo the drunkard out of your luxuriant garden, he begins to mo an ( も ) with distress. Your garden is so luxuriant that the flowers have wrapped their roots around him and started draining the nutrients from his body, causing him to moan in anguish. Hints You can't believe this has happened again. The last drunk to wander in was moaning for a week before the flowers finished draining his life-force. I guess this is just the price you pay for having a luxuriant garden.

meaningMnemonic: Under the same flag , all the people get together to present a new weapon to your lord . You all bow and say, " Milord , this gift is for you." Because that's the proper way to address your lord. Hints When you address your lord you better say "milord," otherwise you might get beheaded with the weapon you're all giving him.
readingMnemonic: As you give the lord his weapon together, you see his face turn into a frown, "What's wrong, Milord ?" you ask. "THERE'S A DEN T ( でん )!" he bellows. Hints Oh no, oh no, oh no! Now the lord is running around with his dented weapon trying to put dents in all of you. You don't want a dent in your head! Run!

meaningMnemonic: When you go to the yakuza to make things straight , your problems just multiply . Hints Why would you ask the yakuza to "straighten out" a problem for you? Do you realize what that means in yakuza-speak? Your problems are going to be multiplying exponentially, friend.
readingMnemonic: Your problems multiply and give you quite a shock ( しょく ) as yakuza thugs commit crime after shocking crime on your behalf. You really shouldn't be shocked though — of course crimes are going to multiply when you ask the yakuza to "straighten things out." Hints Feel shock envelop your entire body as yakuza run around town roughing up everyone who's ever wronged you. Police attention on you is beginning to multiply, too, and you can't even think from the shock of it all.

meaningMnemonic: Inside that building someone is doing a rice dance . That someone is your neighbor . Hints Imagine your neighbor doing a rice dance, whatever that may be, in the building next to yours. That's your neighbor, for ya.
readingMnemonic: Your neighbor has an incredible rin g ( りん ) that they use for their rice dance. Hints Imagine the ring your neighbor has as overly extravagant. You have to make it wild enough for you to remember. Maybe it is integral to their rice dance. Perhaps you covet your neighbor's rice dance ring.

meaningMnemonic: One way to put wheat in your face is with noodles . Hints Imagine yourself shoveling piles of wheaty noodles into your face. They're so wheaty and delicious!
readingMnemonic: Once you're done stuffing noodles in your face, you can use your leftover noodles to make noodle men ( めん ). Hints Did you ever use to make pictures with your food? (Or maybe you still do? We won't judge.) Imagine you're doing that again, and think about how lifelike your noodle men are!

meaningMnemonic: Every winter the thread fields become overgrown . Yes, thread grows in fields these days. And the thread grows the most in the winter because reasons. The thread gets so overgrown that you can’t even walk through it without cutting the thread down with a machete. Hints Imagine trying to wade through this overgrown field of thread. It’s really difficult, and also it’s really cold because it’s winter. You shiver. Imagine chopping the thread down with your machete. Chop chop chop!
readingMnemonic: The reason this field of thread got so overgrown is because you’re Han ( はん ) Solo and you’re not used to simple things like farming thread. Han Solo is used to blasting baddies and kissing princesses. Overgrown thread is not his specialty. Use your blaster to clear a way through this thread instead of using that machete. Hints Imagine yourself as Han Solo, bravely blasting your way through the overgrown thread with your blaster. Pew pew pew!

meaningMnemonic: You're using your scooter to navigate the flood because you're on patrol . You're one of the few people with a floating scooter, so it's your job to patrol the flood waters and look for people and animals that need help. Hints Imagine patrolling the flood waters on your scooter, which is bubbling and scooting along on the surface of the water. You have to be extremely vigilant in your patrol, you don't want any lives to be lost on your watch.
readingMnemonic: You have to patrol all of the floods in June ( じゅん ). Unfortunately, that's the month when most of the floods in Japan happen, so you end up on patrol a lot. Hints You're in a group with a bunch of other scooter people, and you're all assigned to one month of flood patrol duty. But you got June. The floodiest month. Womp womp.

meaningMnemonic: This tree is the master of a pillar . The pillar is subservient to its tree master because the tree is so great and awesome and big and cool and stuff. The pillar has great respect for its tree master. Hints See the pillar next to the tree master. See the pillar bow over and over in veneration of its tree master.
readingMnemonic: While bowing, the pillar accidentally smashes Chew bacca ( ちゅう ). The pillar is horrified for having murdered Chewbacca, his tree master’s closest friend. The pillar is going to be punished. Hints Hear the crack and snap of branches as the tree beats the crap out of the pillar for having murdered Chewbacca. Unforgivable.

meaningMnemonic: Use your fingers to shoo a turkey down the stairs and into a portable carrier. You've been trying to get this turkey into the carrier so you can transport it for like, the past hour. You finally got it done with the help of gravity. And, you know, smacking it a bit in the butt with your fingers. Hints Turkeys aren't portable on their own. I mean you could pick one up I guess, but it will bite and poop on you. So get it in a portable carrier first.
readingMnemonic: You needed the turkey to be more portable because you're going to be bringing it to a ca ke ( けい ) shop to turn it into a cake. You aren't cooking it! Geez, what's wrong with you? No, you're making a cake OF it, for its birthday. The baker needs to see it for reference. Hints Imagine getting a portable turkey cake made of your pet turkey. It's made of turkey friendly cake mix.

meaningMnemonic: Lift the lid off your preserve s, kick it, and praise the lord! Your food is preserved, you don't need the lid anymore, praise be! Hints You also praise the lid. And praise the plants and animals that gave you the food.
readingMnemonic: You do this prais ing in your ho me ( ほう ), though, not a church. I don't think anyone outside your home would understand why you're praising inanimate objects. Hints If you're going to praise the ingenuity of the invention of the "lid" for its preservation methods, you should definitely do it from home. Or at least from the internet from home. Find your people where you can, you know?

meaningMnemonic: A horse is your master and you are merely a resident in his house. How did this horse become your master? Those aren’t questions a resident should ask! Know your place, resident! Hints Imagine having a horse as your master. Hear him neigh out orders to you and the other residents of the horse master’s house.
readingMnemonic: To prove yourself a worthy resident of the horse master’s house, you must capture Chew bacca ( ちゅう ). Your horse master collects rare creatures, and Chewbacca is his latest desire. If you wish to remain a resident of the house, you must capture Chewbacca. Hints Imagine Chewbacca in a cage in the horse master’s house. You’ve proved yourself a worthy resident. Hear Chewbacca making his Wookie sounds as he bashes against the bars of his new cage.

meaningMnemonic: You employ a geoduck to review all your work. Hints Imagine hiring a geoduck, then ask them to review your work. Please review my writing, geoduck. Please review my record-keeping, geoduck. Please review my taxes, geoduck. This geoduck you employed can review anything for you.
readingMnemonic: As the geoduck review s your paperwork, it notices something surprising. You have a 子 ( こ )! Hints The geoduck tells you that while it was reviewing your records, it found information about a child you have. Even you didn't know this, so you're surprised that this review geoduck found something like this.

meaningMnemonic: The cow of righteousness is always there for us. He is the cow that must sacrifice himself for us to survive. Hints The reason he is sacrificing himself is so we can all eat! Yum! Thanks to your sacrifice, righteous cow, we all have hamburgers. You should think about all the cows you ask to die for you every day. Maybe say thanks next time.
readingMnemonic: The sacrifice must be done via gui llotine ( ぎ ). I know, I know, that sounds really brutal, but it's the best way. It's fast, it's effective, and hopefully the sacrifice—I mean, cow—doesn't feel a thing. Hints Of course, the reading is also shared with kanji like 義 . The righteousness radicals seems to have that effect on kanji.

meaningMnemonic: You see an animal with some flowers and a turkey on a stool trying to seize them. The animal with the flowers is really tall so the turkey needs to stand on the stool in its attempt to seize the flowers. Hints Look at this turkey straining itself on the stool trying to seize the flowers, grunting with effort. You think he’ll ever get them?
readingMnemonic: The animal the turkey is trying to seize the flowers from is a cock ( かく ). The cock is a lot bigger than the turkey, so that’s why the turkey needs to stand on the stool in its attempt to seize those flowers. Hints Imagine this scene again only with a big cock holding the flowers as the turkey attempts to seize them. Hear the cock shouting cock-a-doodle-doo as it defends its flowers.

meaningMnemonic: If you have gold you also need a guard with a very sharp sword to protect it. Hints You should probably also get some sharp spikes, sharp traps, and sharp spears to keep that gold safe too. Just a bunch of sharp stuff.
readingMnemonic: You're setting up all these sharp traps around your gold when you step on a sharp a corn ( えい ) that's just lying on the floor. Ouch! But wait, then you get a great idea! Hints Imagine covering the floor around your gold in sharp acorns. This is basically a Home Alone situation, and anyone who tries to steal your stuff is gonna get stuck full of sharp things and probably stabbed by your guard.

meaningMnemonic: Taking a cross with a drop on it, you walk through the rice paddy in the direction of winter and spread your arms wide. You spread your arms to halt the approach of winter because your rice paddy is not done growing yet. You take the cross with you for some extra religious power of persuasion, and the drop in case any of that rice is thirsty. Hints Imagine facing the direction of the approaching winter while facing away from the rice paddy. Feel the weight of the cross in your hands as you spread your arms and implore the winter to hold off on its arrival. Drip the drop onto any thirsty rice.
readingMnemonic: With your arms spread like that, you look extremely chic ( しき ). Spread arms are obviously a chic posture, and the fact that you're holding a cross makes it even more chic. Side note: The official kun'yomi reading is just し , but since far more words use しき , we're focusing on that here. Even though the き part is technically okurigana, it's actually used in the readings for most of the compounds that use this kanji! Hints Feel the strain on your chic arms as you continue to spread them. Since you're by far the most chic person around, you have to set a good example for your people, so don't let them (or your arms) down.

meaningMnemonic: What kind of woman comes down from heaven ? A supernatural one. She is so enchanting . Hints Imagine your idea of what an extremely supernatural woman would look like, and have her come down from heaven towards you. You're totally enchanted by her looks.
readingMnemonic: The supernatural woman comes down in front of you and she's so enchanting that it takes a while to realize she's completely made of yo gurt ( よう ). Hints Touch the supernatural yogurt woman and feel the yogurt. Taste the yogurt, what flavor is it? It's totally enchanting you further.

meaningMnemonic: The scooter you made out of grain s, and are about to ride down the stairs with, is completely transparent . You mashed the grains down so fine that you can see through them! And then you made them into a scooter. Hints Picture this transparent scooter. Well, it's actually a bit hard to see, because it's see-through. I guess imagine the outline and the feel, as you perch at the top of your stairs.
readingMnemonic: You slip, the transparent scooter scoots down the stairs without you and into the streets of とう きょう . Nooo! Transpa-scootie come back! Hints Almost immediately you lose track of the scooter because it's transparent. All you see is とうきょう in front of you. And no scooter. Maybe this is why people don't make transparent vehicles.

Since 贈り物 comes from the verb 贈る , it describes a gift not just as an object but as something given with care. You'll often see it in writing or polite speech when someone wants to emphasize the warmth or sincerity behind a gift.
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 贈る and 物 .

meaningMnemonic: This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What adjective describes something that's been dilute d? Thin , diluted , or faint . 薄い is mostly for flat things, like 薄い紙 (thin paper) or 薄い壁 (thin walls). Stuff without depth, basically, which is why it also extends to expressions like 薄い味 (diluted flavor) and 薄い色 (faint color).
readingMnemonic: You take a sip of your coffee and find it's thin and diluted , so you say, " Ooh, Sue ( うす )… This coffee isn't good." Sue made you this cup of coffee, but as usual, she's made it way too thin and watery. "Ooh, Sue… I hate to break it to you, but this is not drinkable."

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means transparent , so it makes sense that the verb vocab version means to be see-through or to be transparent . 透ける focuses on something being see-through, often because it's thin or sheer, like stockings, lace curtains, or a light-colored shirt. It can also describe something being visible through something else — literally or figuratively — like 模様が透ける (a pattern shows through) or 本音が透けて見える (someone's true feelings show through).
readingMnemonic: I bet you have a lot of things that you wouldn't want to be see-through — and if they were, you'd contact the maker and threaten to sue ( す ). You know, your clothing, the walls of your house, so on. Whoever made all this see-through stuff is getting sued for everything they're worth.
